headers.//: Every response carries the same policy Cloudflare serves from _headers. Kept identical on purpose - a site that is hardened on one host and bare on another is a site whose security depends on which URL somebody happens to open. tools/audittest.js compares the two files and the meta tag in index.html, and fails if any of the three drifts.

headers.//: Images, frames and vendored libraries never change without a new filename, so they can be cached hard. This is what keeps a second visit nearly free against the daily quota.
Scripts and styles DO change, and a stale one against a fresh index.html is how a site half-updates. Revalidate every time; the 304 costs almost nothing.
The shell must never be cached, or a deploy does not reach anyone still holding the old one.
Nothing that touches an account may sit in a shared cache, and nothing about it belongs in a referrer.
